reasoning: Primary-document lane: the Q3 FY27 10-Q, 8-K release and presentation, and the call transcript set the base: Q3 revenue $2,056.3M (+41.6%), Comms $1,614.6M at 12.8% adj. EBITDA margin, Building Systems $441.7M at 23.8%, backlog $12.9B (12-month $6.7B), FY27 revenue raised to $7.66-7.73B. The new information is management's FY28 framing: Comms only mid-single-digit growth because FTTH customers (AT&T, Verizon/Frontier are each >10% of revenue) slow builds, FTTH down y/y but above FY26, offset by DCI (contracted backlog >$2B), copper reclamation and BEAD. Customer primary documents back the cut: AT&T lowered its 2027-28 capital investment to $22-23B/yr while staying on track for 60M fiber locations by 2030; Verizon is routing 10-15M premises to cheaper FWA. I therefore built Comms from four programs rather than taking the guide: FTTH -18%, DCI $550M, copper+BEAD $300M, base +2%, giving +4.7% FY28 and +8% FY29. Building Systems is AI capex (standing file base: $1.84T 2027, +50%) x a capture that falls because union electrician supply limits growth, giving +18% FY28 and +10% FY29, the low end of 'high teens or better'. Margins: Comms 12.5%/12.7%/13.0% adj. EBITDA (the record on comms margin guidance is a miss), BS 21%/19.5%/19%. EPS (ex-amortization, after SBC) ~$17.6/$19.9/$23.3 sits within ~5% of Nasdaq consensus (15.89/18.99/22.37), which is pre-print. Guidance record: two findable annual revenue guides, both beaten, but the beats came from acquisitions and a 53rd week. Valuation: P/E is the lead leg; whole-company peers (MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG, STRL) median 17.1x NTM, DY 10.2x after an 18% print-day fall and -68% from the 52-week high; k=0.8 gives 11.3x. EV/EBITDA cross-check 8.0x. Scenarios move the drivers: P10 FTTH -35% y/y, slow DCI, BEAD slip, AI capex low case, margins -150bp, 8.8x; P90 FTTH flat, faster DCI/BEAD, BS +30%, 14x. Research limited to ~10 searches; FTTH share of Comms is an inference from customer concentration (low confidence).
